<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914440_theRebbe_936" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914440_theRebbe_936__p007">
  <section v="18">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the unity of all Israel as one entity, called Kehilas Yaakov, is not due to a perceived transcendent level but rather an intrinsic, essential unity, and through this the concept of the inheritance of Torah is revealed, where Israel, Torah, and the Holy One are completely one.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And to add,</t>
    <t s="1">that this that all of Israel unite to become one reality,</t>
    <t s="2">Kehilas Yaakov,</t>
    <t s="3">is not because a superiority above division is felt in them</t>
    <t s="4">[in the manner of the unity of Yeshurun, from the term “shir” (song),</t>
    <t s="5">which is through the revelation of the encompassing [light] that is above division],</t>
    <t s="6">for Yaakov is from the term “eikev” (heel),</t>
    <t s="7">and in the heel no superiority is felt,</t>
    <t s="8">but rather an intrinsic unity.</t>
    <t s="9">And likewise regarding the unity of Israel in the matter of dancing with the heels.</t>
    <t s="10">And through the matter of Kehilas Yaakov,</t>
    <t s="11">the matter of “morashah” (inheritance) is revealed,</t>
    <t s="12">the inheritance of Torah,</t>
    <t s="13">[that] Israel, the Torah, and the Holy One, blessed be He, are all one.</t>
    <t s="14">For in the gift of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="15">there are three matters:</t>
    <t s="16">the giver, the receiver, and the gift</t>
    <t s="17">(the Torah),</t>
    <t s="18">but not so regarding the matter of the inheritance of Torah,</t>
    <t s="19">[where] Israel, the Torah, and the Holy One, blessed be He, are all one.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="19">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section states that the drawing down of this inheritance of Torah on Simchas Torah is through great joy, and from Simchas Torah it extends throughout the entire year, leading to a year of delight in Torah study without hindrances, ultimately culminating in the era of Moshiach.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the drawing down of this matter</t>
    <t s="1">(morashah,</t>
    <t s="2">the inheritance of Torah)</t>
    <t s="3">on Simchas Torah,</t>
    <t s="4">is with great joy.</t>
    <t s="5">And from Simchas Torah this is drawn forth upon the entire year,</t>
    <t s="6">that it should be a year of delight in the study of Torah without any hindrances or delays,</t>
    <t s="7">for this reason all of Israel yearn etc. for the days of Moshiach, for then there will be no hinderer or delayer from engaging in Torah and mitzvos, as explained,</t>
    <t s="8">until [it will be] “and the earth will be filled with knowledge of the L-rd as the waters cover the sea,”</t>
    <t s="9">with the coming of Moshiach Tzidkeinu, speedily and truly.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
